text:
Jamie Benn got there. A fifth-round pick in 2007 who has never played for anyone but Dallas, the Stars' captain scored against Buffalo on Saturday for his 1,000th NHL point, after a few nights of the whole building waiting for it. He joins a short list of one-team players to reach the mark, and he did it with an Art Ross Trophy (2014-15) already on the shelf.

At 37 his role is smaller, about 13 minutes a night with no power-play points, but he isn't a ceremonial passenger. Dallas takes 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, more than seven points better than without him, and his four goals and eight points are a fair return on his chances. Three goals in his last ten games is a nice run for a depth forward.

NHL Edge puts his top speed in the 7th percentile, so the game lives around the net now: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting his share of passes across the slot last season. The one old habit Evolving-Hockey flagged is penalties: he takes more than he draws.
